chapterNote: The psalm of the cross. David writes out of a suffering pressed past every ordinary explanation — forsaken yet still saying 'my God,' mocked in the very words the rulers would one day use at Golgotha, bones out of joint, tongue dried to the jaw, hands and feet pierced, garments divided by lot — and a thousand years later his greater Son took the psalm's first line onto His own lips in the darkness (Matthew 27:46). The turn comes mid-verse at verse 21: 'You have answered me.' From there the sufferer becomes the singer, and the psalm widens ring by ring — the brothers in the congregation, all the seed of Israel, the meek who eat and are satisfied, the ends of the earth turning to the LORD, the fat and the dust-bound alike bowing, and finally a people not yet born being told that He has done it. Golgotha's own last word, 'It is finished,' is this psalm's closing line grown up.

1.text: For the choir director, set to 'The Doe of the Dawn.' A psalm of David. My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? Why do You stand so far from saving me, so far from the words of my roaring?
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach — the overseer of the music] upon Aijeleth Shahar ['the hind of the morning', ayyelet shachar, the KJV margin], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. My God [El], my God, why have You forsaken [azab — abandoned, left] me? why are You so far [rachoq] from helping me ['my salvation', yeshuah, the KJV margin], and from the words [dabar] of my roaring?
1.notes: azab (H5800) is full abandonment, and yet the cry holds on with both hands: Eli, Eli — 'MY God' twice, El (H410) the Mighty One. The 'roaring' (H7581) is a lion's word for wordless agony. These are the very syllables Jesus cried from the cross (cf. Matthew 27:46; Mark 15:34).

2.text: O my God, I cry by day and You do not answer, and by night, and there is no silence for me.
2.amp: O my God [Elohim], I cry [qara] in the daytime [yomam], but You hear [anah — answer] not; and in the night season [layil], and am not silent ['there is no silence to me', the KJV margin].
2.notes: anah (H6030) is the answering-word: the daytime qara (H7121) meets no reply, and the night brings no dumiyyah, no quieting of the ache. Unanswered is not unheard — verse 24 will say so — but the psalm refuses to skip the hours where it cannot yet be felt.

3.text: And still You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel.
3.amp: But You are holy [qadosh], O You that inhabit [yashab — sit enthroned upon] the praises [tehillah] of Israel [Yisrael].
3.notes: The pivot-word is 'But': theology holding while feeling drowns. yashab (H3427) is to sit as on a throne — God enthroned on tehillah (H8416), the accumulated praises of His people, a seat built from every past deliverance the next verse remembers.

4.text: Our fathers leaned their trust on You; they trusted, and You brought them out.
4.amp: Our fathers [ab] trusted [batach — leaned their weight on] in You: they trusted, and You did deliver [palat] them.
4.notes: batach (H982), twice: trust as full weight leaned on a support. The sufferer argues from the family record — palat (H6403), the deliverance-word, has never once failed the fathers who leaned.

5.text: They cried to You and were rescued; they trusted in You and were not put to shame.
5.amp: They cried [zaaq] unto You, and were delivered [malat]: they trusted [batach] in You, and were not confounded [bosh — put to shame].
5.notes: Three generations of the same sequence: zaaq (H2199), the cry for help; malat (H4422), the escape; and never once bosh (H954), the shame of a trust that proved misplaced. Which sharpens the agony — why is the pattern breaking on me?

6.text: But I — I am a worm and no man at all, the scorn of mankind, despised by the people.
6.amp: But I am a worm [tolaath], and no man [ish]; a reproach [cherpah] of men [adam], and despised [bazah] of the people [am].
6.notes: The tolaath (H8438) is the crimson worm crushed for scarlet dye — an image the church has long loved here: life crushed out, and covering color for others in the crushing. bazah (H959), despised, is Isaiah's word for the suffering Servant (cf. Isaiah 53:3).

7.text: All who see me mock me; they curl the lip, they wag the head, saying,
7.amp: All they that see [raah] me laugh me to scorn [laag]: they shoot out ['open', the KJV margin] the lip [saphah], they shake [nua] the head [rosh], saying,
7.notes: The mockery is bodily: the sneering saphah (H8193) and the wagging rosh (H7218). The passersby at the cross did exactly this, 'wagging their heads' (cf. Matthew 27:39) — the psalm reads like an eyewitness report written in advance.

8.text: 'He rolled himself on the LORD — let Him rescue him! Let Him deliver him, since He delights in him.'
8.amp: 'He trusted ['rolled himself on', galal, the KJV margin] on the LORD [YHWH] that He would deliver [palat] him: let Him deliver [natsal] him, seeing He delighted [chaphets] in him.'
8.notes: galal (H1556) is to roll: the taunt quotes the sufferer's own faith back at him — he rolled his whole case onto the LORD (cf. Psalm 37:5). The rulers at Golgotha repeated it nearly verbatim: 'He trusted in God; let Him deliver Him now, if He will have Him' (cf. Matthew 27:43).

9.text: Yet You are the One who drew me out of the womb, who made me trust while I lay at my mother's breasts.
9.amp: But You are He that took [giach — drew forth] me out of the womb [beten]: You did make me hope ['kept me in safety', batach, the KJV margin] when I was upon my mother's [em] breasts.
9.notes: The answer to the taunt is biography: giach (H1518), God as the midwife who drew him forth, and batach (H982) learned at the breast before he could name it. The relationship predates his capacity to doubt it.

10.text: I was cast upon You from birth; from my mother's belly You have been my God.
10.amp: I was cast [shalak — thrown] upon You from the womb [recham]: You are my God [El] from my mother's [em] belly [beten].
10.notes: shalak (H7993), thrown — as a newborn is laid on a father's knees to be owned. There has never been a moment of this life outside the claim 'my El'; the psalm's first cry and this verse are the same grammar, possession refusing to let go.

11.text: Do not be far from me, for trouble is near, and there is no helper at all.
11.amp: Be not far [rachaq] from me; for trouble [tsarah] is near [qarov]; for there is none to help ['not a helper', azar, the KJV margin].
11.notes: The geometry of the crisis: tsarah (H6869) qarov, trouble near, and God rachoq, far — the two distances that must trade places. 'Not a helper' (H5826): the field is empty of every aid but One.

12.text: Many bulls have surrounded me; the strong bulls of Bashan have hemmed me in on every side.
12.amp: Many [rav] bulls have compassed [savav] me: strong [abbir] bulls of Bashan have beset me round [kathar — encircled as a crown].
12.notes: Bashan (H1316) bred the heaviest cattle east of the Jordan; abbir (H47) is brute strength. kathar (H3803) is to circle like a crown — the enemies wreathe him, the first ring of a menagerie of predators that now closes in verse by verse.

13.text: They open their mouths wide against me, like a lion tearing its prey and roaring.
13.amp: They gaped ['opened their mouths against me', the KJV margin] upon me with their mouths [peh], as a ravening [taraph — prey-tearing] and a roaring lion [aryeh].
13.notes: The aryeh (H738) mid-kill: mouth open, tearing (H2963) and roaring (H7580) at once. The bestiary is deliberate — bulls, lion, dogs, wild oxen — humanity's cruelty wearing every predator's face in turn.

14.text: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are pulled out of joint; my heart has turned to wax, melted deep inside me.
14.amp: I am poured out [shaphak] like water [mayim], and all my bones [etsem] are out of joint [parad — sundered, the KJV margin]: my heart [leb] is like wax; it is melted in the midst [tavek] of my inward parts [meeh].
14.notes: shaphak (H8210), poured out like a drink-offering; parad (H6504), bones separated — the anatomy of a body suspended by its limbs. The melted leb (H3820): courage, will, and the physical heart failing together. Crucifixion was not yet invented when this was written.

15.text: My strength is dried up like a broken piece of pottery, and my tongue sticks fast to my jaws; You have laid me down in the dust of death.
15.amp: My strength [koach] is dried up [yabesh] like a potsherd [cheres]; and my tongue [lashon] cleaves [dabaq — clings fast] to my jaws; and You have brought me into the dust [afar] of death [mavet].
15.notes: cheres (H2789), the shard of a broken pot — baked dry, good for nothing (cf. 'I thirst', John 19:28). dabaq (H1692) is the cleaving-word of covenant loyalty, here tragically literal. And the final hand is God's own: 'YOU have brought me' — the sufferer sees sovereignty even in the afar mavet.

16.text: For dogs have surrounded me; a band of evildoers has closed in on me. They have pierced my hands and my feet.
16.amp: For dogs have compassed [savav] me: the assembly [edah] of the wicked [raa] have inclosed me: they pierced [karah — dug through] my hands and my feet [regel].
16.notes: The edah (H5712), the assembly-word used of God's congregation, here convened for evil. 'They pierced' — karu, dug through — my hands and my feet: the verse the church has read at the foot of the cross since the beginning (cf. John 20:25; Luke 24:39-40), written centuries before Rome hung its first man on wood.

17.text: I can count every one of my bones, while they look on, staring at me.
17.amp: I may tell [saphar — count] all my bones [etsem]: they look [nabat] and stare [raah] upon me.
17.notes: saphar (H5608), to count one by one: the body stretched until the ribcage stands out ready for counting — and not one etsem broken (cf. Psalm 34:20; John 19:36). The starers make suffering a spectacle; the counted bones make it Scripture.

18.text: They divide my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots.
18.amp: They part [chalaq — divide] my garments [beged] among them, and cast [naphal] lots [goral] upon my vesture [lebush].
18.notes: chalaq (H2505) and the goral (H1486), the lot: executioners gambling over a dying man's clothes. All four evangelists record its fulfillment at the cross, John down to the seamless tunic that could not be divided and so was diced for whole (cf. John 19:23-24).

19.text: But You, O LORD, do not be far away; O my Strength, come quickly to help me.
19.amp: But be not You far [rachaq] from me, O LORD [YHWH]: O my strength [eyaluth], haste [chush] to help me.
19.notes: The covenant name at last: YHWH (H3068), the LORD, invoked for the first time by the sufferer himself since the taunt of verse 8. eyaluth (H360), a rare noun — Strength as a personal title — and chush (H2363), the hurry-verb: the prayer has pared down to 'come fast.'

20.text: Rescue my soul from the sword, this one life I have from the power of the dog.
20.amp: Deliver [natsal] my soul [nephesh] from the sword [cherev]; my darling ['my only one', yachid, the KJV margin] from the power ['hand', yad, the KJV margin] of the dog.
20.notes: yachid (H3173) — 'my only one' — is Isaac's word at the binding (cf. Genesis 22:2): the single unrepeatable life a man has. One nephesh (H5315), one chance, prayed out of the dog's hand.

21.text: Save me from the mouth of the lion — and from the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me!
21.amp: Save [yasha] me from the lion's [aryeh] mouth [peh]: for from the horns [qeren] of the wild oxen [rem] You have heard [anah — answered] me.
21.notes: The hinge of the whole psalm, mid-verse: the prayer 'save me' breaks off into the past tense — anah (H6030), 'You HAVE answered.' Between the lion's mouth and the oxen's horns, deliverance lands. Everything after this line is doxology; the unanswered cry of verse 2 is unanswered no more.

22.text: I will declare Your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will praise You.
22.amp: I will declare [saphar] Your name [shem] unto my brethren [ach]: in the midst [tavek] of the congregation [qahal] I will praise [halal] You.
22.notes: The counting-word saphar (H5608) of verse 17 returns redeemed: the man who counted his bones now recounts God's shem. Hebrews puts this verse directly on the risen Christ's lips — 'I will declare Your name to My brethren' (cf. Hebrews 2:12): the Sufferer leading the singing.

23.text: You who fear the LORD, praise Him! All you seed of Jacob, glorify Him! Stand in awe of Him, all you seed of Israel!
23.amp: You that fear [yare] the LORD [YHWH], praise [halal] Him; all you the seed [zera] of Jacob [Yaaqob], glorify [kabad] Him; and fear [gur — stand in awe of] Him, all you the seed of Israel [Yisrael].
23.notes: Three imperatives ring outward — halal (H1984), kabad (H3513), gur (H1481) — summoning the whole zera (H2233) of Jacob. The delivered man does not keep the deliverance; he conscripts a nation into the singing.

24.text: For He has not despised nor scorned the affliction of the afflicted one; He has not hidden His face from him, but when he cried out to Him, He heard.
24.amp: For He has not despised [bazah] nor abhorred [shaqats] the affliction of the afflicted [ani]; neither has He hid [satar] His face [panim] from him; but when he cried [shava] unto Him, He heard [shama].
24.notes: The theology of the whole ordeal in one verse: bazah (H959), the despising men did in verse 6, God never did. The hidden panim of the opening cry is answered — satar (H5641) negated — and shama (H8085): the day-and-night crying of verse 2 was being heard the entire time.

25.text: From You comes my praise in the great congregation; I will pay my vows before those who fear Him.
25.amp: My praise [tehillah] shall be of You in the great [rav] congregation [qahal]: I will pay [shalam] my vows [neder] before them that fear [yare] Him.
25.notes: tehillah (H8416) — the praises God is enthroned on in verse 3 — now has this deliverance woven into it. The neder (H5088) paid in public was the thanksgiving sacrifice with its shared meal, which sets the table for verse 26.

26.text: The meek will eat and be satisfied; those who seek Him will praise the LORD. May your heart live forever!
26.amp: The meek [anav] shall eat [akal] and be satisfied [saba]: they shall praise [halal] the LORD [YHWH] that seek [darash] Him: your heart [lebab] shall live [chayah] for ever [ad].
26.notes: At the votive meal the anav (H6035), the lowly, eat free — suffering turned into a feast for others, saba (H7646), satisfied. The blessing 'may your lebab live le-ad, forever' reaches past the meal toward the resurrection scope of the psalm's final verses.

27.text: All the ends of the earth will remember and come turning back to the LORD, and every family of the nations will bow in worship before You.
27.amp: All the ends [ephes] of the world [eretz] shall remember [zakar] and turn [shub] unto the LORD [YHWH]: and all the kindreds [mishpachah] of the nations [goy] shall worship [shachah — bow down] before [panim] You.
27.notes: The second ring: from the qahal to the ephes eretz (H657, H776), the very ends of the earth. zakar and shub (H2142, H7725), remember and turn — conversion described as homecoming, and the mishpachah (H4940) of the goyim inherit Abraham's family blessing (cf. Genesis 12:3).

28.text: For the kingdom belongs to the LORD, and He is the ruler over the nations.
28.amp: For the kingdom [melukah] is the LORD'S [YHWH]: and He is the governor [mashal] among the nations [goy].
28.notes: melukah (H4410), the kingship itself: the sufferer of verse 6 announces the reign of God over every goy (H1471). The cross-shaped psalm ends in a coronation — the same arc the gospel takes (cf. Philippians 2:8-11).

29.text: All the well-fed of the earth will eat and bow down; all who go down to the dust will kneel before Him, even the one who cannot keep his own soul alive.
29.amp: All they that be fat [dashen — the prosperous, the well-fed] upon earth [eretz] shall eat [akal] and worship [shachah]: all they that go down [yarad] to the dust [afar] shall bow [kara — kneel] before [panim] Him: and none can keep alive [chayah] his own soul [nephesh].
29.notes: Both ends of the human ladder at one table: the fat of the earth and those already sinking to the afar (H6083) — the dust of death from verse 15, where the Sufferer Himself went. No man can chayah his own nephesh; every knee that bows, bows as a beggar (cf. Romans 14:11).

30.text: A seed will serve Him; it will be told of the Lord to the coming generation.
30.amp: A seed [zera] shall serve [avad] Him; it shall be accounted [saphar — recounted] to the Lord [Adonai] for a generation [dor].
30.notes: zera (H2233), the seed: a posterity the dying man of verse 15 had no natural hope of — offspring by resurrection (cf. Isaiah 53:10, 'He shall see His seed'). saphar (H5608) a third time: counted bones, declared name, and now a story recounted down the generations.

31.text: They will come and declare His righteousness to a people yet to be born: He has done it.
31.amp: They shall come [bo], and shall declare [nagad] His righteousness [tsedaqah] unto a people [am] that shall be born [yalad], that He has done [asah] this.
31.notes: The last ring: a people not yet yalad (H3205), born — every future believer, us included — told one sentence: asah, 'He has done it.' The Hebrew ends in a single completed verb, and its Greek shadow fell from the cross itself: tetelestai, 'It is finished' (cf. John 19:30).
